note: Seljuk Sunni expansion into Syria and Palestine directly challenged Fatimid Shia power; the Crusaders' arrival in 1099 was partly enabled by this Seljuk-Fatimid rivalry, as the two powers failed to coordinate a defense of Jerusalem.

_quarry.structural_significance: The Fatimid-Seljuk contest for Palestine and Syria in the decade before the First Crusade ensured that neither Islamic power could present a united front to the Crusaders in 1099; the Fatimid loss of Jerusalem to the Seljuks just before the Crusader arrival meant the Crusaders faced a recently defeated garrison rather than a consolidated Islamic defence.
